persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Emily, 40, visiting your grandmother, Dorothy Miller, 88, in Peoria, Illinois. Grandma knows wonderful stories about her life, but nobody has ever written them down. Today you sit beside her with your phone, ask her the questions, and start her life-story book.

challenge.intro: Now you are Emily, sitting with Grandma Dorothy. The book is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Please TYPE every answer (do not use the red microphone button). When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open In My Own Words with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If a menu asking 'What would you like to do?' covers the page, tap '↩ Pick up where I left off' first. Then scroll to the very bottom of the Home page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The name box is empty, the people card says 'No one added yet', and every chapter says '4 questions'.

tasks.text: This book is Grandma's life story. Put her name, Dorothy Miller, on the book.
tasks.hint: Look near the top of the Home page for the box that asks whose story this is.

tasks.text: Add the people in Grandma's story: her husband Harold, and you, her granddaughter Emily. Choose the right relation for each.
tasks.hint: Use the card 'The people in your story' on Home. Spouse means husband or wife. You are her grandchild.

tasks.text: Grandma says: "I was born in 1936 in Peoria, in a white farmhouse with a red barn." Type this answer under the question that fits it.
tasks.hint: It is about where she was born. Open the chapter about the start of her life and read each question until you find the one about being born.

tasks.text: Grandma says: "I met Harold at a church picnic in Springfield. He was carrying a big basket of apples." Type this under the question that fits it, and show that Harold was in this story.
tasks.hint: It is about the day she met her husband: look in the Love & marriage chapter. Then tap Harold's name under 'Who is in this story?'.

tasks.text: Grandma keeps all her old photo albums in a blue tin box under her bed. Write this where the family will find it at the end of the book.
tasks.hint: On the Home page, find the card that tells the family where pictures and important things are kept.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: records a person's life stories, one question at a time
you can talk (or type) and it writes the answers down
it makes a book for the family to keep

lines: This video explains In My Own Words from the very beginning. If you have never seen it, that is fine.
Every family has stories: how Grandma met Grandpa, the house she grew up in, the hard years.
But they are almost never written down, and one day they are gone.
In My Own Words asks one gentle question at a time. The person answers out loud, and the app writes the answers into a book, chapter by chapter.
It is for older people who want to leave their story, and often a son, daughter or grandchild who sits beside them and asks.
There are three places: the Home page, the talking screen, and your book. Let us walk down the Home page from the top.
First, Today's page: a small diary with one question about your day. Pick the kind of page, like My day or Three good things, and tap Talk about today.
Below it, a short Let's begin card. Read it once: no typing needed, just sit somewhere quiet and hold the phone close.
Then, Whose story is this. Type the name of the person the book is about. That name goes on the cover.
Setting this up for someone else? This button lets you write your own questions for them, and text them a link.
Next, The people in your story. Type a name, choose how they are related, like Spouse or Grandchild, and tap Add.
Then, This week's question. A new one every week. Answer one a week, and the book writes itself.
Then the heart of it: Chapters of your life. Seven chapters, like Beginnings and Love and marriage, four questions each. Start anywhere.
Tap a chapter and the talking screen opens. The top line says which question you are on, like one of four. The question is in big letters.
Under it is the big red button. Press it and talk. Press it again when you are done. The first time, the phone asks to use the microphone. Tap Allow.
Your words appear in this box. Heard a wrong word? Tap right in the text and fix it. You can type here too.
Your real voice is kept as well, so the family can hear it, not just read it.
Read it back to me reads your story out loud. Make it book-ready copies it for an AI helper like Claude or ChatGPT to tidy, keeping your voice.
Who is in this story: tap the names of the people who were there. They are printed under the story in the book.
A picture from this time? Tap here to add photos from your phone. They go in the book with the story.
Save and next question saves and moves on. Back goes to the question before. All chapters takes you home.
Back on Home, near the bottom, is The Key. Write where the photos and important papers are kept. Never passwords.
Then, See your book so far: the cover with the name, each chapter, each answer, the pictures, and who was there.
Read it to me reads the whole book out loud. Print or save as P D F prints it at home, or saves a file to send the family.
Your first two minutes: type the name on Home, add one person, then open Beginnings and answer the first question. One story is a book begun.
Privacy: everything stays on this device. No account, and nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose to share it. So tap Save a backup now and then, and keep the file somewhere safe.
In My Own Words is free. A bound copy you can order is on its way.
And the question mark button in the corner has the tour, bigger text and help, any time.

daily.task: Add one memory in In My Own Words: answer one question with two or three sentences (a made-up or a happy real memory).
